endorsements.quote: Involving patient advocacy groups, local leaders, and diverse stakeholders in both the design and deployment of these tools is essential to ensure that technologies genuinely reflect the needs and values of the populations they are meant to serve [ 13 ].
Implementing this framework demands a robust Data Governance policy to establish data ownership and ensure compliance with global regulations like GDPR and HIPAA.

unlisted_practices: Embed explainability tools into AI models used in clinical trials and adopt clear reporting standards so stakeholders can understand how conclusions are reached.
Inform trial participants about how their data will be used, what role algorithms play in decisions, and what safeguards protect privacy, as part of informed consent.
Validate and quality-control synthetic data generated by GANs or SMOTE to avoid introducing spurious clinical correlations.
Standardize demographic and diversity variables using clinical data standards such as CDISC SDTM and ADaM.
Conduct pilot studies integrating AI-driven recruitment optimization and bias monitoring into live randomized clinical trials.

Develop clear regulatory standards for evaluating AI in clinical trials for fairness, explainability, and accountability through collaboration among regulators, sponsors, developers, and patient advocacy groups.
Pair AI-driven recruitment with culturally sensitive outreach, accessible language support, and open communication about how the technologies are used.

screen.reason: The paper presents a conceptual framework and recommendations for embedding AI/ML to improve equity, diversity, and inclusion in clinical trial design and monitoring rather than an empirical evaluation.
